Combine burns of consecutive slices of a collection

Source: R/cb_combine.R
cb_combine.Rd

Concatenate cb_burn() results that share a grid and whose geometry ids do not overlap, as when a collection is burned in chunks (one per worker, say) with id_offset set to the number of geometries before each chunk. The result is the same, record for record, as burning the whole collection at once: each geometry's records are produced independently, so joining the chunks in id order changes nothing.

Usage

cb_combine(...)

Arguments

...

cb_burn objects, or a single list of them. They may be given in any order; the tables are joined in order of id_offset.

Value

A cb_burn object on the shared grid. Its id_offset is the lowest of the inputs' and n_geom spans to the highest id, so if the chunks leave a gap in the ids those geometries count as empty. parent is kept when all inputs agree on it.

Details

All inputs must have identical extent, dimension, crs, coverage and (for cb_burn_index() burns) geotransform, and their id ranges (id_offset, id_offset + n_geom] must not overlap, and either all or none must have a relations table; otherwise an error is raised rather than silently merging different geometries under one id.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(wk)
g <- wkt(c("POLYGON ((1 1, 4 1, 4 4, 1 4, 1 1))",
           "POLYGON ((5 5, 9 5, 9 9, 5 9, 5 5))"))
grid <- list(extent = c(0, 10, 0, 10), dimension = c(10, 10))
a <- cb_burn(g[1], extent = grid$extent, dimension = grid$dimension)
b <- cb_burn(g[2], extent = grid$extent, dimension = grid$dimension,
             id_offset = 1)
cb_combine(a, b)
} # }
